identity.title: Sulphur monoxide exposes a potential molecular disk wind from the planet-hosting disk around HD 100546

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first detection of SO in the planet-hosting disk around HD 100546 from ALMA Cycle 0 observations gaining insight into the molecular content and structure of transition disks.

evidence.quote: HD 100546 is a $2.4~M_\odot$ Herbig Be star (cite: Ancker1998) at a distance of $109^{+~4}_{-~3}$ $pc$ (cite: Gaia1; Gaia2)

question.value: Is SO detectable in the planet-hosting transition disk HD 100546, where is it located, and does it trace a disk wind?

evidence.quote: We present the first detection of SO in the planet-hosting disk around HD 100546 from ALMA Cycle 0 observations gaining insight into the molecular content and structure of transition disks.

method.value: Image each line, shift spw to SO line frequency with regridspw, concat in uv plane, CLEAN natural weighting at 1 km/s

evidence.quote: These measurement sets were then concatenated using the CASA task `concat`.

key_parameters.value: Only 7_7-6_6 and 7_8-6_7 stacked; 8_8-7_7 excluded since it increased noise

evidence.quote: Including the $J=8_8-7_7$ transition in the stacking increased the noise level in the channel maps thus degrading the S/N in the resulting images.

validation.value: Checked velocity frame, line frequencies, removal of 5-10% of baselines, and image-plane stacking; double-peaked profile persists

evidence.quote: we checked the removal of 5% to 10% of the longer and shorter baselines and the double-peaked line profile persists.

analysis_steps.goal: Moment maps of disk and wind components

method.value: Moment zero maps over -7.5 to -2.5 km/s (wind) and -2.5 to 4.5 km/s (disk)

evidence.quote: Figure 4 shows the integrated intensity maps from -7.5 km s$^{-1}$ to -2.5 km s$^{-1}$ and from -2.5 km s$^{-1}$ to 4.5 km s$^{-1}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Matched filter detection and relative line intensities

method.value: Cross-correlate uv visibilities with CO image (scaled to 1/4) and best-fit LIME model as filters

evidence.quote: We use the CLEAN image of the CO line ($J=3-2$) and the best fit LIME model (see Section 5 for details) as filters.
We tested different CO filters with different compression factors of 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4.

validation.value: Compared different filters; response consistent for 7_8-6_7

evidence.quote: We found that the $J=7_8-6_7$ transition is picked up in all the filters but the higher excitation lines have an improved response with the more compact filters.

evidence.quote: The line ratios of the three lines were calculated over a grid of temperatures and densities and the results are shown in Figure 7.
assuming an SO column density of 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ motivated by full chemical models

evidence.quote: A set of models were run varying the fractional abundance of SO with respect to H$_2$.

evidence.quote: These conditions result in the SO being distributed in a ring from 20 to 100 au in a layer above the mid-plane

evidence.quote: The critical density for the SO $J=7_{7}-6_{6}$ transition was determined to be $6~\times~10^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$ at 100 K

findings_qualitative.value: SO emission is more compact than CO and has an excess blue-shifted component not consistent with Keplerian disk emission, attributed to a disk wind

evidence.quote: The blue-shifted emission peaks off source spectrally and spatially and it is attributed to a disk wind

findings_qualitative.value: Disk SO emission is asymmetric, peaking north-east, coincident with CO hot-spot and possible warp

evidence.quote: This is coincident with a ‘hot-spot’ observed in CO emission relating to a possible disk warp (cite: walsh2017).

claims.hypothesis: Is SO detectable in the HD 100546 disk?
claims.experiment: Imaging, uv stacking and matched filtering of Cycle 0 Band 7 data
claims.result: Two lines detected in image plane; three detected with matched filter
claims.finding: First detection of SO in HD 100546 disk

evidence.quote: We detect SO in the protoplanetary disk around HD 100546 for the first time.

claims.hypothesis: Does SO trace a molecular disk wind?
claims.experiment: Line profile and moment map analysis, comparison with CO
claims.result: Blue-shifted off-source component at about -5 km/s
claims.finding: SO may trace a molecular disk wind

evidence.quote: In addition, we have shown that SO may be a tracer of a molecular disk wind.

claims.experiment: LIME models of full disk and wedge
claims.result: 5e-6 wrt H2 for wedge, above dark cloud value ~1e-8
claims.finding: Energetic processes may release refractory sulphur

evidence.quote: This suggests that there are energetic processes occurring in HD100546 releasing a source of refractory sulphur into the gas phase.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Accretion shock from a circumplanetary disk as alternative explanation

evidence.quote: An alternative explanation for the SO emission is that it is the result of an accretion shock due to a circumplanetary disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Emission is the same size as the beam so disk and wind components cannot be disentangled; model kinematics mismatch

evidence.quote: Further refinement of the disk emission component requires better data as the emission is the same size scale as the beam.

referee_caveats_inferred: Detections are low S/N (5-7 sigma) near beam size, so wind interpretation is tentative
Wedge position chosen by eye and abundance degenerate with density
Matched-filter ratios used as intensities with large errors
Blue-shift could have other explanations, e.g. warp
